title: Management of post-COVID syndrome in a university outpatient clinic or day-care hospital setting
summary: In some individuals, symptoms persist after a COVID-19 infection. These symptoms do not resolve even after the acute infection has subsided and can last for an extended period, a condition referred to as post-COVID syndrome (PCS). To track the development of certain factors over time and to gain a better understanding of this condition in a PCS-affected patient population, patients from the PCS outpatient clinic and day clinic at UKSH in Kiel are being studied in the PCS CARE study.

interventions.name:
Patients with post-COVID syndrome are assessed at defined time points as part of routine care:

• Medical history (anamnesis)
• Blood analyses
• Questionnaires
• Functional assessments (sit-to-stand test, handgrip strength, pulmonary function testing, neurological assessment)

Some parameters

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with PCS who are connected to the PCS outpatient clinic or day clinic at UKSH, Campus Kiel.
Current residence in Schleswig-Holstein or Hamburg.
Bell Score of at least 30.
For participation in the PCS therapy group: sufficient physical capacity, individually assessed by a physician.
Written or electronic informed consent from the participant.
Exclusion criteria:
For participation in the PCS therapy group: exercise intolerance that is likely to prevent successful participation.
Residence outside of Hamburg or Schleswig-Holstein.
Bell Score below 30.
